verdicts.evidence: Confirmed end-to-end, current main. extract.ts:830-833 stamps EVERY `kind: 'action'` operation (the extractor's category for state-mutating functions) with `safe: false` unconditionally ('action → false per §4'). That `op.safe` is threaded through orchestrator.ts buildDescriptor Step 5 into `fnSchema.safe` (entrypoint/apigen-cli/src/lib/orchestrator.ts:588 `safe: op.safe`). compose-schemas.ts:231-232 then computes: `const safe = fnSchema.safe === true || isPrimitiveOnlyInputSchema(fnSchema.input);` — because `false === true` is false, an explicitly-unsafe action with only primitive/enum params (string/number/boolean/integer, or zero params) is unconditionally re-stamped `x-apigen-safe: true`. Every HTTP transport's shared verb resolver (`httpVerb()`, apigen-engine-naming/src/lib/naming.ts:206-214, and `project()`'s identical inline form at naming.ts:150-151 `op.safe || isPrimitiveOnlyInputSchema(op.input) ? 'GET' : 'POST'`) reads that stamp with no kind-awareness, so both apigen-plugin-api-express/src/lib/generate.ts:107 and apigen-plugin-api-fastify/src/lib/generate.ts:126 emit `router.get(...)`/`app.get(...)` for it, and the run.ts live-server paths mount it the same way via the same `buildOpPlan`. The generated GET handler still calls `dispatch(...)` against the real mutating function (generate.ts:127/149) — so a bare GET (browser prefetch, `` CSRF, HTTP cache, proxy auto-retry) executes the mutation. This is not a stale/theoretical path: apigen-plugin-api-fastify/src/test/plugin.spec.ts:834-841 deliberately keeps `parityOpUnsafePost`/`parityOpMultiSegment` non-primitive specifically 'isolating this fixture to the ROUTE-shape regression rather than also exercising FEAT-APIGEN-022's GET auto-hoist' — i.e. the test authors themselves knew and worked around the fact that an unsafe action WITH primitive params would get hoisted to GET. compose-schemas.spec.ts's `verb-safe.1/.2` tests (lines 486-494) assert the hoist fires with no explicit `safe:true` present, which is exactly the shape every real extracted `action` produces (safe is always explicitly `false`, never `undefined`, so the OR-hoist is never actually gated by kind in practice).
verdicts.recommendedAction: Real, live, currently-tested-and-working-as-implemented behavior — not decayed. This needs an architecture decision, not a one-line patch: the OR-hoist (`fnSchema.safe === true || isPrimitiveOnlyInputSchema(...)`) treats an EXPLICIT `safe:false` from an action-kind operation identically to an unset/unknown safety signal, so param shape alone can override an extractor's explicit unsafe classification. Options an architect should choose between: (a) gate the auto-hoist so it only applies when `fnSchema.safe` is `undefined` (never for an operation the extractor explicitly marked `kind:'action'`/`safe:false`), requiring the existing manual `--opt http.verb.<id>=GET` override to force GET on a mutation; (b) keep the hoist but require callers to declare mutation-safety explicitly per-op and treat absence as unsafe-by-default; (c) accept current behavior but mandate CSRF-safe-by-construction guarantees (e.g. require a non-GET-forgeable header) before allowing GET-mounted actions. Recommend routing to architect lane given the CSRF/prefetch/cache/proxy-retry security implications of executing mutations via bare GET.

verdicts.evidence: Reproduced live against the currently-shipped dist (entrypoint/backlog/dist/package.json version 0.1.8, matching CHANGELOG.md's latest 0.1.8 entry — not stale). Root cause: query.ts's listItems()/queryItemNodes() (entrypoint/backlog/src/store/query.ts:90-101) passes filter.limit/filter.offset straight into the SQL-level NodeFilter (nodeFilter.limit/nodeFilter.offset), but the open/closed status filter is a PURE post-hoc JS filter applied AFTER that SQL page comes back (query.ts:39-43 applyOpenClosedFilter, called at query.ts:100 from listItems, i.e. after queryItemNodes already sliced the page). nodeFilterFromBacklogFilter (query.ts:16-37) only writes filter.status into the SQL metadata match when status is a real terminal/open BacklogStatus value — for the common 'open'/'closed' meta-values it adds nothing to the SQL WHERE at all, so the SQL page is drawn from the UNFILTERED (open+closed intermixed) row order, then status-filtered afterward. I proved this drives the item's exact symptom with a standalone repro against the built dist (via require of dist/index.js, a real consumer-shaped call, not a bypass): 30 items in repo debug-repro/bug-backlog-003b, pattern = 5 open, 20 closed (contiguous run > page size), 5 open. listItems({repo,status:'open'}) with no pagination correctly returns all 10 open items (ground truth). But paginating with limit=10/offset stepped by 10: offset=0 -> 5 open items; offset=10 -> 0 items (the whole raw window at that offset is the closed run); offset=20 -> the remaining 5 open items. A caller using the standard 'stop when a page comes back empty/short' pagination convention stops at offset=10 and permanently loses the last 5 open items — exactly 'paging past [a boundary] silently returns a wrong, overlapping, incomplete window'. I also confirmed the companion half of the claim ('offset is not honored'): in @adhd/sox-graph-store's installed queryNodes (node_modules/@adhd/sox-graph-store/dist/index.js:1213-1220, version 0.8.4, the version this repo's backlog package.json pins as ^0.8.4), the OFFSET SQL clause is only appended INSIDE the `if (filter?.limit !== undefined)` branch — passing offset with no limit silently drops the offset entirely. Repro confirmed this too: listItems({repo, offset:5}) with no limit returned all 30 rows, not 25. Neither the BUG-020 singleton-writer-lock fix nor the sox-store-adapter 0.5.8->0.7.0 bump (CHANGELOG.md 0.1.8 entry, read in full) touch pagination/query logic at all — they're about writer-lock and WAL durability, an unrelated layer — so this item was never incidentally fixed by that work. There is also zero test coverage for limit/offset in entrypoint/backlog/src/store/query.spec.ts (grep for offset/limit/paginat returned nothing), consistent with this shipping unnoticed. I could not independently confirm the specific '~145 rows' number since I have no backlog MCP tools in this session to observe a live large-repo listing, but the underlying mechanism (SQL-level page slicing happening before an in-memory status filter, plus the graph-store's offset-requires-limit gap) is real, current, and reproducible right now — the qualitative claim in the title is fully verified live regardless of the exact magic number.
verdicts.recommendedAction: Scoped fix belongs entirely in entrypoint/backlog/src/store/query.ts. When filter.status is 'open' or 'closed' (the meta-filters applyOpenClosedFilter handles), queryItemNodes must NOT push limit/offset down into the SQL-level NodeFilter (since the status filter that will run afterward can't be expressed as a SQL-level metadata equality — nodeFilterFromBacklogFilter's own comment at query.ts:28-30 already documents this exclusion). Instead, fetch the full status-unfiltered node set for the other filter dimensions, apply applyOpenClosedFilter, THEN slice by offset/limit in JS — the file already has exactly this precedent for the grep branch at query.ts:87 (`if (filter.offset) live = live.slice(filter.offset);`), so the non-grep branch (query.ts:90-95) needs the equivalent treatment gated on `filter.status === 'open' || filter.status === 'closed'`, plus a `.slice(0, filter.limit)` for the limit half. Separately (smaller, upstream): sox-graph-store's queryNodes should append `OFFSET ?` even when `filter.limit` is undefined (e.g. by defaulting to `LIMIT -1 OFFSET ?` in SQLite) — that's outside this repo (an @adhd/sox-graph-store fix, sox-ecosystem repo, out of scope for this backlog run), so entrypoint/backlog callers should treat 'offset without limit' as unsupported/reject-or-default-a-limit until that's fixed upstream. Add regression coverage in query.spec.ts driving exactly the 5-open/20-closed/5-open contiguous-run shape used in this repro, asserting the full offset-swept page set equals the unpaginated status='open' ground truth.

verdicts.evidence: Root cause confirmed by reading the schema-generation pipeline: packages/apigen/apigen-core-client/src/lib/schema-builders/morph-walk.ts (index-signature branch, ~line 9670) renders `Record<string, unknown>` as `{type:'object', additionalProperties: <schema for `unknown`>}` with NO `properties`/`required` constraint (fully permissive — matches ANY object), and the `unknown`/`any` fallback (same file, just above `detectDiscriminator`) renders as `{}` (also fully permissive). `detectDiscriminator` (same file) requires EVERY branch to have `type:'object'` AND `properties`; the catch-all branch has no `properties` at all, so it returns `undefined` — no discriminator is attached for a `T | Record<string, unknown>` union, exactly as the bug claims. Then reproduced END-TO-END with REAL components (no mocks): started a real `mcpPlugin.run()` HTTP-streaming MCP server (from @adhd/apigen-plugin-mcp, real code) exposing a tool whose output schema is the union shape this pipeline produces (`oneOf: [{type:object, properties:{outcome,hits}, required:[...]}, {type:object, additionalProperties:{}}]`, no discriminator — exactly mirroring the composed-schema shape the real extraction pipeline emits, per the file:line above), connected a REAL `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` `Client` over `StreamableHTTPClientTransport`, called `listTools()` (which populates the SDK's real ajv-backed output validator per node_modules/@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/dist/esm/client/index.js's `cacheToolMetadata`), then called the tool with its real, correctly-shaped result. The REAL SDK client threw: `MCP error -32602: Structured content does not match the tool's output schema: data/result must match exactly one schema in oneOf` — the value legitimately matches BOTH the domain branch and the permissive catch-all branch simultaneously, which JSON-Schema `oneOf` (enforced by ajv, node_modules/@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/dist/esm/validation/ajv-provider.js, standard strict:false config which still enforces oneOf exclusivity) rejects. This is exactly the -32602 error code and 'every real result fails' mechanism the bug describes. Also confirmed by absence: packages/apigen/apigen-plugin-mcp/src/test/run.spec.ts's only BUG-APIGEN-019/output-schema test (lines 524-544) uses a union where EVERY branch shares a literal discriminator tag (`outcome: 'found'|'empty'`) — a case that legitimately resolves a discriminator and is NOT ambiguous — and contains zero references to `additionalProperties`, `catch-all`, or `ambiguous` (grep-verified), so the actual `T | Record<string, unknown>` catch-all scenario this bug describes is untested in the current suite.
verdicts.recommendedAction: Genuine, currently-live bug with real client-visible impact (-32602 on every matching result). Needs an architecture decision on how to model a T | Record<string,unknown> (or any union with a fully-permissive catch-all branch) in `normalizeTopLevelUnion`/`detectDiscriminator` (apigen-core-client) so the emitted `oneOf` isn't self-ambiguous for MCP's outputSchema — e.g. reorder/rewrite as the domain branch only (treat the catch-all as 'anything else, don't advertise a schema for it'), or drop to `anyOf` for MCP's outputSchema specifically (accepting looser validation) while keeping `oneOf`+discriminator for other transports that don't ajv-validate output. verdicts.evidence: No `.close()` call and no try/finally exist anywhere in the real-runner production path. entrypoint/dispatch-cli/src/lib/core.ts:231-251 (runCycleCore) and :346-373 (calibrateCore) both build `buildProductionAgentMcpRunner()` (a real AgentMcpRunner spawning `npx -y @adhd/agent-mcp` via StdioClientTransport, packages/dispatch/dispatch-orchestrator/src/lib/agent-runner.ts:304-324) and never close it. entrypoint/dispatch-cli/src/api.ts:150-198 (run/calibrate) are pass-throughs with no cleanup. `grep -n 'process.exit\|\.close()' entrypoint/dispatch-cli/bin/cli.ts` returns only `process.exit(1)` inside `fail()` at line 57 — no `.close()`, no finally, no SIGINT/SIGTERM handler in the whole file. agent-runner.ts:446-450's own doc comment says close() is 'not part of IDispatchAgentRunner... callers and tests own this lifecycle step,' but the only caller that does it is test-only code: entrypoint/dispatch-cli/src/test/integration/real-e2e.ts:990-1084 (`finally { if (runner) await runner.close(); }` on a runner it constructs itself for the test).
verdicts.recommendedAction: Root cause confirmed and scoped more broadly than the title: the leak happens on EVERY real invocation (success or failure), not just early exit — because printAndExit() in bin/cli.ts never calls process.exit(0), a successful `dispatch-cli run --no-dry-run`/`calibrate` will hang forever (spawned child's open stdio pipes keep the event loop alive), and on the `fail()` error path the child becomes an orphan since process.exit(1) doesn't tear down non-detached spawned children. Fix: wrap the real-AgentMcpRunner branches of runCycleCore/calibrateCore (or their bin/cli.ts callers) in try/finally calling runner.close(), and add process.exit(0) after a successful printAndExit(). Ready to hand to architect/devops for the actual patch — this is a clear, scoped fix, not a design question.

verdicts.evidence: Live reproduction against a real temp SQLite-backed GraphBacklogStore (no mocks), via a scratch script driving the real client API (openTmpStore + client.createItem/softDeleteItem/auditTrail from entrypoint/backlog/src). Output: `CASE2 auditTrail after softDeleteItem: THREW BacklogItemNotFoundError backlog item not found: PseudoSky/backlog-softdelete-check::BUG-SOFTDELTEST-001`. Root cause traced to two files: (1) entrypoint/backlog/src/store/query.ts:117-124 `findItemNode` resolves (repo,humanId)->node exclusively via `store.graph.queryNodes(...)`; (2) node_modules/@adhd/sox-graph-store/dist/index.js:1210-1213 `queryNodes(filter)` calls `buildNodeFilterClause(filter, true, 'n')` with `liveOnly` HARD-CODED `true`, which (index.js:571-577) always appends `t_invalid IS NULL` to the SQL WHERE clause — so an invalidated node can never come back from queryNodes, period, regardless of caller intent. `softDeleteItemNode` (entrypoint/backlog/src/store/crud.ts:412-421) invalidates via `store.graph.invalidate(node.id, reason)`, which stamps `t_invalid` (confirmed at index.js:1131 `UPDATE node SET t_invalid = ? ... WHERE rowid = ?`). Once that lands, `auditTrail` (query.ts:364-402) calls `findItemNode` at query.ts:365, gets `null`, and throws `BacklogItemNotFoundError` via `buildNotFoundError` at query.ts:366 -- exactly reproduced above.
verdicts.recommendedAction: IMPORTANT CITATION CORRECTION for whoever specs this: markdown.ts:306 ('the graph node itself is NEVER deleted... full history remains queryable via auditTrail') is inside `buildChangelogSection`, and documents `archiveResolved`'s behavior specifically -- NOT `softDeleteItem`'s. I ran the archiveResolved path too (CASE1 in the same repro): `CASE1 auditTrail after archiveResolved: SUCCESS, history entries=3` -- that documented capability is 100% intact and not what's broken. The real, reproduced defect is narrower and different: `softDeleteItem` (the actual soft-delete/invalidate path, distinct from archive) makes a node permanently unreachable by `auditTrail` because the only lookup path (`findItemNode` -> `store.graph.queryNodes`) is hard-liveOnly at the @adhd/sox-graph-store layer -- there is no `includeInvalid` escape hatch on `queryNodes`. Two viable fix shapes for the architect to choose between: (a) add an invalidated-node lookup in backlog's own query.ts using `store.adapter` raw SQL directly (crud.ts:402-404 already does raw `store.adapter.executeRun` for a similar reason, so there's local precedent), scoped so ONLY `auditTrail` bypasses liveOnly -- everything else (listItems, findItemNode's other callers) should keep filtering deleted items out; or (b) extend @adhd/sox-graph-store's `queryNodes`/`NodeFilter` with an explicit `includeInvalid` option (bigger, cross-package change, needs a version bump and a look at every other queryNodes call site in that package to confirm nothing else silently starts leaking invalidated rows). Route to architect: this is a real, reproducible bug, but the fix has a genuine design fork (local workaround vs. upstream package API change) that needs a decision before speccing.
